Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're putting together our security questionnaire for legal and InfoSec and have a short set of clarifying questions specific to data residency, retention, and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. Please see the attached questionnaire (Acadia_retention_questionnaire_v2.pdf) and the inline questions below — we'd like responses we can include in our vendor risk assessment.

Key clarifying items:
- Does Redwood store request/response payloads persistently for hosted API customers by default? If so, where (region) and for how long?
- What is the retention policy for log data vs. model telemetry vs. customer-submitted training data?
- Describe the deletion/erasure flow for a data subject request and estimated SLA to complete in hosted mode. Does deletion purge backups/snapshots?
- Any options for region restriction (e.g., storing tenant data only in us-east-1) or geo-fencing for hosted customers?

We're on a tight timeline — would appreciate your answers by EOD Friday so we can close the vendor review.

Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. I've drafted initial responses below and attached a concise PDF we typically share with customers (redwood_acadia_answers_v1.pdf). I've also looped in Marissa (Product) and Monica (Support/Privacy) for any operational clarifications.

Quick summary (high level answers):
1) Do we store request/response payloads persistently by default?
- Answer: By default, Redwood's hosted API keeps per-request telemetry (metadata, diagnostics, and model-level logs) for 30 days. Request/response payloads are not persisted long-term unless a customer enables explicit data retention (e.g., for evaluation or analytics). For customers who opt in to longer retention, data is stored in the customer's configured region for the duration of the retention window.

2) Retention policy differences (logs vs telemetry vs training data):
- Logs / access logs: 90 days by default for hosted customers, can be extended via enterprise add-on.
- Model telemetry (usage metrics, token counts, latency traces): 30 days by default; aggregated telemetry longer-term for platform health (anonymized).
- Customer-submitted training data / stored prompts: Only stored if customer uses our storage/monitoring features or uploads assets; retention follows the customer's configured TTL and default is 365 days unless otherwise agreed.

3) Deletion / erasure flow and SLA:
- For hosted customers, deletion requests are handled via our support portal and automated workflows. Standard SLA: 7 business days to complete a tenant-scoped erasure (remove data from primary stores). Additional 21-30 days to account for cross-region replication and immutable backups; we provide attestations when complete.
- Backups: Snapshots and cold backups are rotated and encrypted; we mark data for purge and exclude from future restores. Final removal from all durable backups may take up to 30 days depending on retention windows.

4) Region restriction / geo-fencing:
- Hosted customers can request data residency constraints; for many customers we can restrict tenant data to a single region (e.g., us-east-1) at onboarding. Some controls require Dedicated/Private deployments for strict guaranteed isolation; hosted residency is best-effort and configurable at account creation.

I've attached the fuller Q&A doc with references to our data flow diagram and deletion checklist. If this looks good, happy to send the formal response for Acadia's vendor packet.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Elena / Acadia Security team — thanks for the patience. Attached are our formal responses and a short data flow diagram for the hosted API environment. Below is a concise, customer-ready summary you can include in your vendor packet.

Official Redwood response (concise):
- Default persistence: Redwood does not persist customer request/response payloads beyond diagnostics/telemetry unless the customer opts into storage features. By default, telemetry retained 30 days; access logs retained 90 days.
- Storage location: For hosted customers, tenant data is stored in the cloud region selected at account creation. At onboarding, we can request/reserve the following regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1.
- Retention tiers: logs (90 days), telemetry (30 days), customer-submitted artifacts (configurable; default 365 days).
- Deletion / erasure process: Tenant-scoped erasure requests initiated via support result in primary-store purges within 7 business days. Cross-region replication and immutable backup rotation can add up to 30 additional calendar days before final removal from all durable snapshots. Customers receive an attestation document when purges are complete.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups are encrypted and subject to lifecycle policies; after a deletion request we mark data as ineligible for restore and schedule removal per retention rotation.
- Residency controls: We support region restriction options for hosted accounts at onboarding. For strict legal/regulatory residency guarantees, Dedicated or Private deployment options are recommended.

Attachments included: redwood_acadia_answers_v1.pdf (detailed Q&A), redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (service boundaries and residency notes).

If you'd like, we can add a short deletion attestation signed by our Compliance team once you confirm this language.
